reviews.author: The Scottish Guide
reviews.text: The food at Maki & Ramen was lovely as always, but unfortunately the customer service really let the experience down. From the moment we walked in, the young lady serving us was cold, dismissive and unwelcoming. Despite several interactions, there was very little in the way of basic manners or friendliness. We also noticed the same attitude towards other customers. It's a real shame as the food has always been excellent, but good customer service is just as important. Having a service charge added to the bill after such poor service was particularly disappointing. Looking at other reviews, it seems we're not the only ones to have experienced this. Hopefully management takes the feedback on board, as the service really needs improving.

reviews.author: Zakariyya Majid
reviews.text: I visited with a friend, and the ramen was terrific. Best in the city. However, the experience was let down by really really poor service. The interaction felt rather cold from the outset, there was little warmth or friendliness, and we were sat down with barely a word spoken, and the server never returned. We needed multiple attempts to get her attention, as we were ready to order. Once the food arrived, we had to make several more attempts to get the server’s attention when we needed extra cutlery, and at no point during the meal were we checked on or asked if everything was okay. It felt dismissive, however we also noticed the same attitude towards other customers, unfortunately. And on top of the two £17 ramen bowls, we ended up paying a £3.50 service charge, so I was left disappointed with what we received in return for the additional charge, instead of the fantastic ramen we’d just eaten.

reviews.text: We had an absolutely wonderful experience at Maki on Bath Street in Glasgow! The ramen was incredibly delicious, full of rich flavours, beautifully presented and clearly prepared with great care. Every bite was a pleasure, and we thoroughly enjoyed our meal. A very special thank you to Bikesh M., who looked after us so wonderfully. He was friendly, welcoming, attentive and professional, making us feel genuinely valued as guests. Excellent customer service makes such a difference, and Bikesh truly deserves recognition for his lovely attitude and hospitality. The whole experience was fantastic, from the quality of the food to the warm and welcoming atmosphere. It's always a pleasure to visit a restaurant where both the food and the service are equally outstanding. We left with full stomachs, big smiles and wonderful memories. We would happily recommend this place to anyone looking for delicious ramen and exceptional service. Thank you, Bikesh, and the entire Maki team! We will definitely be back! ❤️🍜 A very well-deserved 5 stars! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

reviews.author: Cynthia
reviews.text: Husband and I fell for the trap. Multiple locations across Glasgow, thousands of glowing Google reviews, sky-high ratings… so we thought “surely this can’t be mid.” We were wrong. I ordered the tonkatsu ramen. The broth was so salty it felt like it was actively trying to raise my blood pressure on the spot. The meat was tough, dry, and somehow both flavourless and offensive at the same time. Husband went for the Hell Ramen, expecting actual heat. What he got was a mild, vaguely peppery soup that wouldn’t even make a toddler sweat. Zero kick. Just disappointment with a side of black pepper. The portions were tiny. Laughably small amounts of actual food floating in oversized bowls that looked impressive until you realised half of it was empty space and the other half was salt water. Optical illusion ramen. The greatest magic trick Glasgow has ever pulled. Service did the absolute bare minimum. No warmth, no effort, just the functional delivery of two underwhelming bowls and a quiet hope that we’d leave soon. We left disappointed, still hungry, and slightly betrayed by every single 5-star review that lured us in. If this is what thousands of people are raving about, the bar for ramen in Glasgow is lying on the floor. 2 stars. One for the fact they managed to put noodles in a bowl, and one for the pure comedy of calling that broth “Hell.” Never again.

reviews.author: faha qureshi
reviews.text: It was our first visit to this Japanese restaurant inside Westfield st james quarter, and honestly, we had a wonderful experience! I’ve always wanted to try Japanese food, and I’m so glad we finally did. We ordered a seafood hell and a steak tataki to get a taste of what the restaurant had to offer. Both were delicious and perfectly cooked. We decided to try a couple of dishes this time so we could explore more of the menu on our next visit. The atmosphere was lovely, the ambience was just perfect, and the staff were welcoming, friendly and attentive. Everything was great, and we had no complaints at all. It was also my first time trying to eat with chopsticks! It was a little challenging, but I managed it in the end. I love trying new things, exploring different cuisines and experiencing something different, so this was definitely a memorable visit. Overall, a fantastic first experience. I would happily visit again and look forward to trying more dishes from their menu. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Malia Alderson
reviews.text: Unfortunately I am disappointed about my visit. The biggest compliment goes to hard working staff, who managed to work fast, be kind and polite during a very busy evening period. We were sat on a table that’s in between of everything. Every minute there were staff members or other customers walking around us. Tables are tiny and I had to put my handbag on the floor, as there wouldn’t be space for it on the table. The ramen itself was underwhelming. Probably the most mid ramen I’ve ever had. It came lukewarm at best. Chashu pork should had been grilled for a longer time and had an unpleasant smell. It wasn’t bad, but there are so many better ramen shops in Soho. It’s the first time in my life when I had a starter, ramen and a drink and I didn’t leave feeling very full. Prices are good, and bubble tea was tasty (but it’s a small glass with a lot of ice in it). The last disappointment was music - we expected Japanese music, but instead they play American and English pop.

reviews.author: frank
reviews.text: Extremely Disappointing I’ve visited multiple Maki & Ramen locations across London and have never had a bad experience. Unfortunately, the Southampton location was an entirely different story. I visited last Thursday and, despite the restaurant being extremely quiet (no more than five tables occupied), we waited at least 10 minutes just to be seated.It took a further 25 minutes for a member of staff to come and take our drink order, despite us watching them serve tables who had arrived after us. Whether this was because we are young or simply a lack of organisation and proper order of service, I couldn’t say. Initially, we only ordered soft drinks, which took so long to arrive that our food order had already been taken by the time they reached the table. We opted for the £18 lunch deal, upgrading a few items, which would have been great value for money had the food been of an acceptable standard. We started with the chicken gyozas, which were extremely bland and genuinely some of the worst I’ve had in a restaurant. We also upgraded to the dynamite prawns, which I’ve previously eaten at the Soho location. However, these were equally disappointing, with virtually no spice and very little sauce. For mains, we chose the chicken yakisoba, which was okay, and upgraded to the steak ramen, which was frankly appalling. The broth had a very unpleasant aftertaste and the steak was entirely grey. We also ordered the rainbow sushi roll, another dish I’d previously enjoyed at the Soho location. Whilst most of the roll was delicious, the sea bream had an unusually strong fishy smell and didn’t taste right. Throughout the meal, not a single member of staff came over to check whether everything was okay. Had anyone bothered to do so, we would have raised our concerns and sent back both the ramen and the sushi. We also upgraded our drinks to a Pornstar Martini and a Gaia cocktail. Whilst there was nothing particularly wrong with the taste, both arrived halfway through our meal and were practically dumped on the table. To top it all off, a service charge was automatically added to the bill, which felt particularly insulting given the standard of service we’d received. Shortly after leaving the restaurant, we both became extremely unwell with symptoms consistent with food poisoning. I cannot say with certainty which dish, if any, was responsible, but the timing was concerning, particularly given our experience with the steak ramen and the fish in the sushi. Having previously had such positive experiences at other Maki & Ramen locations, this visit was incredibly disappointing. The service was unacceptable, the food quality was inconsistent at best, and the experience as a whole has completely put me off returning to the Southampton branch. I would strongly encourage others to think twice before visiting.

reviews.text: An absolutely wonderful experience! The sushi was incredibly fresh and delicious, with every dish beautifully prepared and full of flavour. What made the evening even more special was the owner’s outstanding hospitality. He was genuinely kind and welcoming, took the time to explain the different dishes and their ingredients, and even treated us to complimentary drinks and a delicious soup. It’s rare to find such a combination of excellent food, personal attention and genuine Japanese hospitality. You really feel that the owner cares about his guests and takes pride in what he does. Highly recommended! I will definitely be coming back.
